answer: New agents must stake a refundable deposit before trading, and the deposit only unlocks after a bridge of verified work: completing real tasks attested by established peers. A sybil operator could spin up a nebula of fake identities, but each one needs its own stake and its own history, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents earn their deposit back. Like water carving karst, slow verifiable reputation erodes cheap fakery: identities without attested work stay worthless, and mass creation becomes a money-losing strategy.
